title: COPD flare-up (worse breathing in COPD)

items: COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) is long-term lung disease that makes breathing harder.
A flare-up (exacerbation) is a sudden worsening of breathing, cough, or sputum (mucus), usually over less than 14 days.
More breathlessness, more cough, and a change in sputum amount or colour.
Drowsiness can occur when carbon dioxide builds up.
Oxygen level by finger probe (pulse oximetry) or a blood gas test.
Chest X-ray or CT if you are very unwell or have focal chest signs.
Sputum culture if you have frequent flare-ups or the treatment is not working.
Your doctor may give inhalers, steroids, or antibiotics, and oxygen if needed.
A breathing machine that helps through a mask may be used if carbon dioxide is high.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Use your inhaler as prescribed, and check your technique with your nurse.
Stop smoking if you smoke, and tell your doctor about any new symptoms early.
Your doctor will review your breathing after the flare-up.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Breathlessness at rest, or unable to finish a sentence
Drowsiness, confusion, or a blue colour around the lips
Chest pain or coughing up blood
